article.title: Hindi to English: Shopping context
article.description: Hindi: 'क्या आपके पास इसका बड़ा साइज़ है?' English: 'Do you have this in a bigger size?' Teaching point: natural English phrasing avoids literally translating 'बड़ा साइज़' as 'big size' — native speakers say 'a bigger size' or 'a larger size'.
article.content: Hindi: 'क्या आपके पास इसका बड़ा साइज़ है?' English: 'Do you have this in a bigger size?' Teaching point: natural English phrasing avoids literally translating 'बड़ा साइज़' as 'big size' — native speakers say 'a bigger size' or 'a larger size'.

Ever asked for a "big size" while shopping? 🤔 While understandable, native speakers usually say "a bigger size" or "a larger size." It sounds more natural!

So next time, try: "Do you have this in a bigger size?"

slides.body:
When asking for a larger item in a shop, the Hindi 'बड़ा साइज़' might tempt you to say 'big size' in English. However, this is a common mistake! Native English speakers almost never use 'big size' in this context.
Instead, the natural and correct phrasing is to use the comparative form: 'a bigger size' or 'a larger size'. So, to ask 'क्या आपके पास इसका बड़ा साइज़ है?', you should say, 'Do you have this in a bigger size?' Remember to use 'bigger' or 'larger' to sound natural and accurate when shopping.
